Figure 3 shows this configuration in detail and Figure 4 shows a 3-D rendition of this arrangement connected to a typical semi-submersible platform. The hull column in the center, which houses the turbine generator and the refrigerant system, is the part that is physically connected to the facility with large steel brackets. This mounting concept is explained in Bailey et al.’s patent application (Bailey 2013). The middle hull column extends to the operational deck of the platform for personnel access. Although the estimated weight of the add-on structure is approximately 310 T (metric tonnes), it has ballast tanks 11 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 at the bottom that ensure self-buoyancy. The actual weight added to the platform weight is that of the supports that are welded to the platform structure (estimated at approximately 20 metric tons). Figure 3: Medium Add-On Configuration The installation of the add-on OTEC plant is envisioned as a subsequent installation after the primary semi-submersible platform, which will include the welded-on supports for the eventual OTEC plant addition, is moored. The add-on would be deployed separately, up righted and submerged to the depth necessary to align with the connection points, and then structurally connected to the semi-submersible platform. After connecting the two structures, the ballast would be adjusted to apply a small downward load on the main structure to aid in stability at the connection. Lastly, the large water lines, including the very long CW Intake pipe, can be connected to the OTEC plant using divers and/or ROV equipment. After the two structures are connected permanently, the power lines and instrument cables could then be connected between the two structures, integrating the power systems and control systems that allow control from the host platform and bi-directional 12 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 power supply.3 The net power produced from the OTEC can be supplied to the host’s power grid. This simplified concept of the OTEC plant allows for the condenser and evaporator to be located on the outside of the additional OTEC hull column, minimizing the risk of flooding in the add-on hull column in the case of a water leak from a heat exchanger.
